newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi determined to be in EMU first group.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi determined to be in EMU first group.

text.p: Italian prime minister Romano Prodi has reiterated his government's determination to be among the first group of nations to enter a single European currency.

Prodi was reported in Italian newspapers on Sunday expressing his confidence that Italy would be ready for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), while he told journalists in Bologna that despite German public opinion against Italy joining EMU, he was resolved to see Italy in the first wave of EMU entrants.

Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported Prodi as saying on Italy's EMU entry, "We will be there." Corriere Della Sera reported, "We will be in the leading group" and in La Repubblica Prodi said, "Italy will enter soon, on this there is no doubt."

Prodi has stressed that sceptism about Italy's ability to meet the Maastricht criteria and join EMU in the first group was now decreasing, and he has said one of the main benefits in making the first round of EMU would be the reduction in long-term interest rates that would result.
This would be particularly useful as interest payments on Italy's hefty debt currently constitute the largest burden on the Italian budget.

Prodi, speaking outside his home in Bologna, was reported by news agency ANSA to have said: "The position of the Italian government is very clear. We have planned a policy to permit us to enter into Europe (EMU) in the first round. This is our policy, the other roads we do not share."
